{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Master Services Agreement

**To:** Deal team  
**From:** In-house counsel (Customer side)  
**Re:** Playbook review of the Master Services Agreement — verified findings

---

## Executive summary

We have reviewed the Master Services Agreement against the playbook. The agreement is, on the whole, strongly favourable to us: 17 of the 19 rules reviewed are compliant, including all of the critical protections on indemnification (§ 20) and intellectual property and Customer Data ownership (§ 14), plus assignment and change of control (§ 24), licence scope (§ 13), termination for convenience (§ 9.4), transition assistance and data return (§ 11), warranties (§ 19), audit rights (§ 22), renewal economics (§ 8) and Vendor insurance (§ 18). There is no exclusivity, non-compete, non-solicit, MFN or minimum-volume obligation binding us, and the only MFN in the document (§ 7.6) runs in our favour.

Two issues require redlines, and both sit in walk-away territory as drafted:

1. **Limitation of liability cap base (§ 21.1) — critical.** Section 21 is structurally sound (mutual cap, mutual exclusion of indirect damages, robust Excluded Claims in § 21.3), but "Fees" is defined at § 1.5 as only the "Implementation Fee", which § 1.6 fixes as a one-time USD 12,000 charge in the first Order Form. Section 21.1 narrows the base further to that first Order Form. Recurring subscription and services charges are excluded, so the cap is an illusory USD 12,000 — below our six-month floor. We propose resetting the base only; mutuality, the damages exclusion and every carve-out are untouched.
2. **Customer-payable liquidated damages (§ 7.7) — low severity, high commercial bite.** Section 7.7 imposes liquidated damages on us of fifteen percent of annual Fees per week for a ten-day payment delay. This is a payment-delay charge, not an early-termination fee, so it cannot fit the fallback (early-termination fee capped at three months' fees), and it would exceed remaining contract value within weeks. Our redline flips the operator so no liquidated damages or penalty is payable by Customer, leaving the surrounding mechanics and the interest treatment in § 7.3 untouched.

## Findings

| Severity | Rule | Status | Section |
|---|---|---|---|
| Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability: cap, mutuality and carve-outs | **Deviation** | § 21 Limitation of Liability |
| Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Compliant | § 20 Indemnification |
| Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Compliant | § 14 Intellectual Property and Deliverables |
| High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Compliant | § 24 Assignment and Change of Control |
| High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity obligations binding Customer | Compliant | § 12 Customer Responsibilities |
| High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Compliant | § 13 Access Rights and Licence |
| High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete restrictions on Customer | Compliant | § 12 Customer Responsibilities |
| High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Compliant | § 9 Termination |
| Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant | § 22 Audit Rights |
| Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Compliant | § 28 Governing Law and Dispute Resolution |
| Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation obligations burdening Customer | Compliant | § 7 Fees, Invoicing, and Taxes |
| Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions | Compliant | § 2 Agreement Structure and Scope |
| Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation of employees binding Customer | Compliant | § 12 Customer Responsibilities |
| Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice window | Compliant | § 8 Term and Renewal |
| Medium | TRANSITION — Post-termination transition assistance and data return | Compliant | § 11 Transition Assistance and Data Return |
| Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Compliant | § 19 Warranties |
| Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Compliant | § 18 Insurance |
| Low | LD — Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer | **Deviation** | § 7 Fees, Invoicing, and Taxes |

## Walk-away items

Both deviations are identified as walk-away territory and should be treated as conditions of signature:

- **§ 21.1 — illusory liability cap.** The cap base resolves to a one-time USD 12,000 Implementation Fee under the first Order Form, excluding recurring subscription and services charges and falling below the six-month floor. Our position: limb (a) reset to fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim, plus a USD 1,000,000 limb (greater of), and confirmation in § 21.3 that Customer's payment obligations are not damages (preserving the existing "undisputed" and "conforming Services" qualifiers as an inclusive example).
- **§ 7.7 — Customer-payable liquidated damages.** Fifteen percent of annual Fees per week triggered by a ten-day payment delay would exceed remaining contract value within weeks and is triggered by a minor breach. Our position: no liquidated damages or penalties payable by Customer.

## Next steps

1. Issue the two redlines to Vendor with playbook comments: the § 21.1 cap-base reset (with the § 21.3 confirmation) and the § 7.7 flip. We will note in each comment that mutuality, the damages exclusion, all Excluded Claims and the § 7.3 interest treatment are unchanged.
2. Confirm with the commercial team the annualised fee run-rate so the 12-month/USD 1,000,000 formulation is calibrated before it goes out.
3. Flag to Vendor that both items are gating for signature; no other rule requires a redline, which should make the ask straightforward to close.
4. On execution, diarise the § 8 renewal mechanics (30-day opt-out, 60-day Vendor reminder) and the § 11 transition window so we can rely on them operationally.
"}
